PLAYING THE GAME 
The following section summarizes the mechanics of the  100DOS 
Game Series . This section also covers a player’s capability when 
interacting with the environment and game mechanics. The first thing 
to get to know is the game’s use of dice. 
 
WHAT IS 100DOS 
100DOS is a Basic Roleplay (BRP) offshoot similar to many other D100 
game systems. 100DOS molded many aspects of tabletop game 
systems into a modular D100-only game built to offer as many choices 
as possible to the Players and the GM. 
 The most important aspect of 100DOS is its Opposed Tests 
system, which is the backbone of character interaction, for both 
combat and social situations. 
 
USING GAME DICE 
This Tabletop game uses a D100 dice system. This dice system is called 
100DOS, or “100 Degrees of Success.” When using this system, the 
users need at least two ten -sided dice. 100-sided dice will not work . 
Dice can be acquired through online stores, local game and hobby 
shops, and even through some bookstores. Make sure to get a pair of 
D10s, where one dice shows the ‘ones’ and the second dice shows the 
‘tens’. 
 Some weapons in this system call for a “dice pool.” Dice 
pools are where a surplus of dice will be needed to determine copious 
amounts of damage. These can be handled by rolling one at a time or 
rolling sets of dice at once. Each of these dice are called Damage Dice. 
 100DOS uses two distinct types of dice rolls, the “D10” and 
the Percentile roll. It is important to note that when the rules say roll 
2D10, this is different from  rolling a percentage roll. When rolling 
1D10, 2D10, and so on, you simply add the results of each die. 
Meaning when you are told to roll 1D10, you roll a single Ten-Sided 
die, and when told to roll 2D10, you roll two Ten-Sided die. 
 Use the following chart as a straightforward way  to 
remember how to use dice rolls. 
 
D10 D5 D10 D5 
1 1 6 3 
2 1 7 4 
3 2 8 4 
4 2 9 5 
5 3 10 5 
 
PERCENTILE EXAMPLES 
EXAMPLE “TENS DIE” “ONES DIE” 
01 00 1 
11 10 1 
10 10 0  
18 10 8 
75 70 5 
100 00 0 
 
NATURAL DICE ROLLS 
A Natural Dice Roll, or Nat, is an outcome of a dice roll that was not 
altered by Bonuses and Penalties. A Natural (Nat) 1 is a dice roll that 
rolled a 1, not a roll that was altered to become 1 using a Penalty or 
Bonus. This applies to any numbers rolled on dice. 
 
WHAT IS ROLEPLAYING? 
In a roleplaying game (RPG) you create an alter ego in a fictional 
setting. This is your viewing glass to another world, as you control and 
help shape out a world with your actions. In a game such as this, you 
are able to create anything your heart desires ; A courageous leader, 
a medical technician, or even a war-hardened master of combat. The 
leader of the game, otherwise known as the Game Master (GM) 
unfolds the story for their players, keeping them intertwined in a 
narrative and combat driven adventure. As a player, choose your 
actions and speak your character’s mind, deciding the path in which 
your party travels. The decisions you and your friends make directly 
affect the events of the story, so be wary. 
 Roleplaying games such as Halo Mythic provide a structure 
of rules that depict how to design your character and control the 
character within the game. Rules are provided to permit shoot -outs, 
powerful battles, chase scenes, and even conversations and 
investigations. These rules require one of two things, dice rolls or 
roleplaying while performing an action. Dice rolls add the factor of 
chance while roleplaying adds the human element of performing 
simple actions or narrative exploration. 
 At the beginning, RPGs like 100DOS appear to have many 
rules. However, you will spend enough time with the system to realize 
that the rules are simple and easy to remember. To judge these rules, 
the GM makes their decisions and decides how difficult something 
should be. The GM usually does not control a character; they instead 
control the game itself. The G M runs the game and presents a story 
as it unfolds about the characters. Consider the G M a roleplaying 
referee and narrator. 
 
WHAT YOU NEED TO PLAY 
When you are ready to start playing, you will need the following 
equipment: 
• Mythic and any other compatible 100DOS Book. 
• The included character sheets or online VTT. 
• Around three or more hours of game time. 
• Some ten-sided dice or a dice rolling program. 
• Paper and Pencil or a computer. 
• A GM and two or more players. 
• Food, Drinks, etc. 
 
You should easily be able to find ten-sided dice. If at any point you are 
unable to find these dice, there are online dice rollers. If you have 
access to a printer, you can make copies of the character sheets given 
with the game. Make sure to print them out for each player. 
 You can help visualize the actions and progress in the game 
by finding suitable miniatures to portray characters. 
 
VIRTUAL TABLETOPS 
Virtual Tabletops (VTT) allow people to play tabletop RPGs online with 
robust and useful toolsets. The two officially supported VTT options 
are Roll20 and Foundry. For Roll20, look for the 100DOS system and 
feel free to check out the automated Mythic Compendium! For 
Foundry, look for Mythic , the officially supported 100DOS 
compendium. Compendiums are automated toolsets that making 
running and playing a game much easier. This includes automated 
dice rolling, bestiary entries, equipment, and much more. 
 
USING TACTICAL MAPS AND GRIDS 
GMs can use visual aids to help track positions and directions. This 
can be accomplished using simple sketches on paper or dry -erase 
boards, preprinted gaming mats and grids, or tactical combat maps 
made to any scale needed. 
 The following is a Table that has recommended grid sizes 
for combat and map scenarios. 
 
RECOMMENDED GRID SIZES GRID SQUARE SIZE IN METERS 
Small Scale - Indoor Fights 1m x 1m 
Outdoors - City Fighting 2m x 2m 
Tactical - Long Range Fighting 5m x 5m  
Vehicle - Long Range Combat 10m x 10m 
Strategic - Large Scale Battles 100m x 100m

TESTS AND DICE ROLLS 
Tests are the main way of determining a Character’s Success or 
Failure. There are many points in which the game will call for a Test 
to be made. The following section shows how these are performed. 
 
THE CORE TEST MECHANIC 
• Determine the Characteristic being used. 
• Apply any necessary Skills or Educations to the Characteristic. 
• Add or Subtract any relevant Modifiers, including those from 
Equipment, Abilities, and Difficulty Modifiers. 
• The final number is what needs to be rolled under to guarantee 
Success on the Test made using a D100. 
• If the percentile is less or equal to the final number being Tested, 
the Test Succeeds and a Degrees of Success will  be gained. 
• If the percentile is greater than the final number being Tested, 
the Test fails and a Degrees of Failure will be gained. 
 
CHARACTERISTIC TESTS 
Characteristic Tests are used by selecting one of the Character’s 
Characteristics that fit the type of Test being made. For example, the 
game may require a Character to make a Toughness Test to avoid an 
undesirable consequence.  
When making the Test, any listed Bonuses, Penalties, or 
Difficulty Modifiers must be applied to the Characteristic for this Test 
and then a D100 is rolled. If the roll is less than or equal to the 
Characteristic after the modifiers were applied, the Test is Successful. 
If the roll is higher, the Test fails. 
 
SKILL TESTS 
Skill Tests are when a Characteristic is enhanced by a Skill, increasing 
the chances of the Test being Successful. Each Skill is managed by a 
set of possible Characteristics that can be used. For example, the 
Character’s Intellect Characteristic can be used for the Medical Skill. 
 Trained Tests will allow you to perform the Skill Test, while 
+10 and +20 Skill Tiers will give Bonuses to the Test, increasing the 
likelihood if succeeding on the Test. 
 
ROUNDING NUMBERS 
Always round numbers down unless specified otherwise. 
 
DEGREES OF SUCCESS AND FAILURE 
Tests that are made will result in either Success or Failure. Degrees of 
Success and Degrees of Failure show how well someone passed or 
how poorly someone failed. 
 Measuring Degrees of Success and Failure is 
straightforward. After the Test is made, you compare the roll made to 
the modified Characteristic. For every 10 points below the modified 
Characteristic, you gain 1 Degree of Success. For every 10 points 
above the modified Characteristic, you gain 1 Degree of Failure. 
 
CRITICAL SUCCESS 
A Critical Success is what happens when a Natural 1 is rolled on any 
Test using the D100. Critical Successes will automatically Succeed Skill 
and Characteristic Tests with a minimum Degrees of Success equal to 
the Characteristic Modifier of the Characteristic being used. 
 Attacks that make a Critical Success will always deal 
maximum Damage, counting as rolling all 5s on a D5 or 10s on a D10. 
You also get to decide where any To Hit Attack would strike. 
In an Opposed Test. If two Characters roll Critical Successes, 
the roll with the most Degrees of Success wins the Test. 
 
CRITICAL FAILURE 
A Critical Failure happens when a Natural 100 is rolled on any Test 
using the D100. Critical Failure s automatically fail any and all Tests  
and the GM should find a punishment befitting.  
OPPOSED TESTS 
Opposed Tests allow Characters to perform competing Tests such as 
Evading an Attack being made, or to spot an Opponent using 
Camouflage. 
 In the Opposed Test, both Characters make their Test. The 
Character who has the highest Degrees of Success will win the 
competing Tests. If both characters gain the same number of 
successes, the character with the highest Characteristic Mod of that 
Test wins. If the results are still a tie, each opponent makes a roll of 
1D10. The highest roll wins. 
 Failed Tests during Opposed Tests can’t succeed, regardless 
of if the Opponent also failed their Test, even if they failed with more 
Degrees of Failure, unless specified otherwise. 
 
BONUSES AND PENALTIES 
Bonuses are beneficial increases to a Test being made, while Penalties 
are detrimental decreases to a Test being made. There are times 
where a Bonus or Penalty is listed as Stacking. Stacking Bonuses and 
Penalties will occur multiple times, adding up each time. Examples of 
this include Evasion Tests, which give a Stacking Penalty with each 
use. 
 
TEST DIFFICULTY 
Not all Tests are equal. Some are much more difficult based on many 
scenarios that could happen, such as landing a Falcon compared to 
landing that Falcon in a hail of gunfire. Test Difficulty is a modifier that 
can set the stage for the type of pressure or the type of test the 
Character is performing. The GM decides how difficult the Test is. 
 If the GM thinks a Test will be “Difficult” to perform, the 
Test will be at a -10. If the GM thinks that this is a trivial Test that you 
should rarely ever fail, it would be at a +60. If there is a Test the GM 
feels like should rarely ever be successful under the given 
circumstances, this Test would be Hellish and at a -60 Penalty. 
 
DIFFICULTY MODIFIER DIFFICULTY MODIFIER 
Trivial +60 Difficult -10 
Elementary +50 Hard -20 
Simple +40 Very Hard -30 
Easy +30 Grueling -40 
Routine +20 Punishing -50 
Ordinary +10 Hellish -60 
Challenging +0                   This is the most common Test you will use. 
 
MYTHIC CHARACTERISTICS AND DIFFICULTY 
When A Character has a Mythic Characteristic that can be applied to 
a Test, they are able to reduce the Penalty by 10 for each +1. For 
example, if a Character has +3 Mythic Strength and is given a -60 
Penalty for forcing a hatch open, they’ll get to reduce the Penalties by 
30. These benefits can’t be gained in an Opposed Test. 
 Mythic Characteristics can’t ignore or reduce Penalties 
given by Medical Effects of any kind, including Special Damage Effects, 
broken and fractured limbs, missing limbs, Flood infection, etc. 
 
ASSISTING WITH A TEST 
A Character may assist another during a Test  by using a Combined 
Action while in Structured Time, or by roleplaying the interaction in 
Narrative Time. 
Each Character rolls the Test using the same Difficulties  
given. The main Character performing the Test will gain a n extra  
Degree of Success to their Test for every Degree of Success an 
Assisting Character gained on their Test. 
 The GM may decide how many Characters can assist in an 
Action. Some examples could be that 4  or more Marines could work 
together in taking down a Brute in Grapple combat, or a couple 
Civilians could work together to fix a radio beacon.

CHARACTER RULES 
 
CHARACTERISTICS 
Characteristics represent your Character’s capabilities within four 
groups: Physicality, Combat, Mentality, and Personality. Each of these 
four groups represent a set of Characteristics  and the Character’s 
potential as a percentage  for each. Characteristics can’t go below 0 
but can rise above 100. 
 Characteristics can be upgraded using Experience (p. 51), as 
well as purchasing Equipment to improve Characteristic Tests. 
 
BASE CHARACTERISTICS 
Base Characteristics are the Characteristics that a Character will begin 
with before Creation Points are spent . For example, a Human will 
begin with all Characteristics at 25, while other Soldier Types may 
begin with more to signify a difference in capability. 
 
CHARACTERISTIC MODIFIERS 
Characteristics have an accompanying Characteristic Modifier that is 
the tens digit of any Characteristic under 100. For example, a 
Characteristic of 54 will have a Characteristic Modifier of 5. 
 If a Characteristic is 100 or above, it uses the Tens and 
Hundred Digits to figure the Characteristic Modifier. A Characteristic 
of 115 will have a Characteristic Modifier of 11. 
 
LOW CHARACTERISTICS 
When a Characteristic is reduced to 10 or lower, the Character will 
gain drawbacks. Each Characteristic will list its own drawback , which 
the GM may replace or allow substitutions for the sake of roleplaying 
and Character building. These are never meant to be  major 
Characteristic or Test Penalties, but instead situational drawbacks for 
both roleplaying and the Actions the Character might take. 
 If a Character’s Base Characteristics began under 10, the 
GM may decide to ignore these Low Characteristic drawbacks. 
 
CHARACTERISTICS REDUCED TO ZERO 
Characteristics reduced to 0 will automatically fail any Tests using that 
Characteristic. The Characters may revert permanently reduced 
Characteristics between Missions with an Extended Medical Test. 
 
PHYSICALITY 
STRENGTH (STR): 
Strength is the physical prowess your Character possesses. Used for 
situations like Melee damage or climbing. 
A Character with a Strength Characteristic of 10 or lower 
will struggle to lift, push, and Oppose Strength Tests. Unopposed 
Strength Tests will take twice as long to perform and the Character 
will gain a Fatigue on failed Opposed Strength Tests. 
 A Strength of 0 can’t Lift, Carry, or Push any objects  and 
can’t deal damage using Melee Attacks.  Weapons can’t be braced, 
and any Attacks made will cause the Character to drop the Weapon 
at the end of their Turn. 
 
TOUGHNESS (TOU): 
Toughness is the Character’s resistance to Damage and debilitating 
effects. Toughness is also used to figure Wounds. 
 A Character with a Toughness Characteristic of 10 or lower 
will struggle keeping themselves healthy and reduce their ability to 
survive various effects. Any time the Character has to make a 
Toughness Test due to a negative effect, the Character will stagger. 
This causes the Character to lose their next Half Action of their Turn. 
 A Toughness of 0 puts the Character into a Coma that can’t 
be awaken from until the Character’s Toughness has been restored , 
not including benefits given by Equipment and Armor. 
 
AGILITY (AGI): 
Agility measures the character’s speed and reflexes. These are used 
when dealing with speed, movement, and evasion. 
 A Character with an Agility Characteristic of 10 or lower will 
have them struggling to keep up with others. If the Character has to 
Run or Sprint, they must make a +15 Agility  Test. If Failed, the 
Character will fall Prone. An Agility of 10 or lower also removes the 
Character’s capability to use Agility for the Stunt Skill. 
 An Agility of 0 prevents all Movement Actions  until the 
Characteristic has been restored, not including benefits from 
Equipment or Armor. 
 
COMBAT 
WARFARE RANGE (WFR): 
Warfare Range is the measurement of the character’s ability to use 
ranged-based weaponry in combat. 
 A Character with a Warfare Range Characteristic of 10 or 
lower will make it impossible to make Called Shots or Aim Actions 
with ranged weapons. 
 A Warfare Range of 0 prevents all Attacks made to a Target 
unless the Target is Helpless and Point Blank to the Character. 
 
WARFARE MELEE (WFM): 
Warfare Melee is the character’s ability to use melee -based 
weaponry and hand-to-hand combat. 
 A Character with a Warfare Melee Characteristic of 10 or 
lower will make it impossible for the Character to  make Called Shots 
or Aim Actions with melee weapons. 
 A Warfare Melee of 0 prevents all Attacks made to a Target 
unless the Target is Helpless and Point Blank to the Character. 
 
MENTALITY 
INTELLECT (INT): 
Intellect is the amount at which characters know and the wisdom the 
character owns. 
 A Character with an Intellect Characteristic of 10 or lower 
will struggle with problem solving. If a Character has to use their 
Intellect Characteristic, they will struggle to solve it in a timely 
manner, even if a Test was needed and was Successful. The Character 
will take twice as  long to solve or respond to things that would take 
this Test. 
 An Intellect of 0 will cause the Character to be unable to 
make any Actions and can only be slowly lead around by another. The 
Character struggles to think and will not be able to respond to 
questions, make most any Actions like Swimming, Running, or 
Climbing, or make Attacks. 
 
PERCEPTION (PER): 
Perception describes the ability to survey their surroundings and 
determines the Character’s Perceptive Range (p. 21). 
 A Character with a Perception Characteristic of 10 or lower 
will struggle with understanding their senses , if their senses are still 
working properly. The Character will not be able to understand the 
direction or estimate the distance of sounds and smells. The 
Character’s eyesight will struggle to see or notice anything outside of 
their Perceptive Range. 
 A Perception of 0 will leave the Character with no capability 
of understanding their surroundings.  They can’t oppose Camouflage 
or Athletics Tests involving sight and sound and making Attacks is at 
a -40 Penalty before any other Penalties are figured.

===== PAGE 8 =====
8 
  
COURAGE (CRG): 
Courage reflects the character’s ability to withstand horrors and fears 
and to keep a clear state of mind. 
 A Character with a Courage Characteristic of 10 or lower will 
find it very difficult to keep their composure. Even slight scares will 
send the Character fleeing for their first Half Action. 
 A Courage of 0 will cause the Character to panic in any 
situation, even if only minorly trying , causing them to always go last 
in every Initiative , as well as  lose every Opposed Test with an 
Opponent who is within Melee Reach. 
 
PERSONALITY 
CHARISMA (CHA): 
Charisma is the character’s ability to interact with other characters 
and players and understanding social cues. 
 A Character with a Charisma Characteristic of 10 or lower 
will be left struggling to understand social cues and scenarios. When 
being spoken to, these Characters will take longer to respond or 
attempt to speak properly. Any time it would have taken to speak or 
respond, the Character will take double the time. If a Character 
needed to quickly warn someone of som ething, they would either 
panic for words before describing the situation, or stutter before 
being able to speak. This also includes the Character st ruggling to 
understand what is said to them, at times. 
 A Charisma of 0 will leave the Character unable to Speak 
and struggle to understand what is spoken to them. 
 
LEADERSHIP (LDR): 
Leadership is the character’s ability to lead forces and to take orders. 
 A Character with a Leadership Characteristic of 10 or lower 
will struggle to understand and give orders. When giving orders, the 
Character will take twice as long a Full Action longer to come up with 
or give the necessary information. The Character will a lso take a Full 
Action before fully understanding the Leadership information needed 
unless it is worded very carefully. 
 A Leadership of 0 makes it impossible for the Character to 
understand or to give orders of any kind. 
  
MYTHIC CHARACTERISTIC 
A Mythic Characteristic is one that is well above what would be 
considered ordinary. Mythic Bonuses give Characteristic 
advancements when figuring character Stats. 
 
Mythic Strength: 
Increases the Character’s Strength Modifier for figuring Melee 
Damage and Carry Weight. (X) Is the character’s Mythic Strength 
Bonus. For figuring Carry Weight, (X) is multiplied by 10, this means 
you add +10 to figuring Carry Weight for a Mythic Bonus of +1. 
  
Mythic Toughness: 
Increases character’s Toughness Modifier when figuring Damage 
Resistance, Carry Weight and Wounds. (X) Is the character’s Mythic 
Toughness Bonus. For figuring Carry Weight, (X) is multiplied by 10, 
this means you add +10 to figuring Carry Weight for a Myth ic Bonus 
of +1. 
 
Mythic Agility: 
Increases character’s Agility Modifier when figuring Movement Speed 
by (X), where (X) is the Character’s Mythic Agility Bonus. It also 
increases the Character’s Initiative Rol l by (X), where (X) is their 
Mythic Agility halved, rounding down, to a minimum of 1. 
 
HEIGHT AND WEIGHT 
A Character’s Height and Weight are decided by the Player or GM and 
allows the Players to immerse themselves with their Characters and 
to better play the Character they created within the world. It also 
allows the GM to use these aspects in their stories whenever needed. 
 
SIZE CATEGORY 
Size dictates Melee Reach, To Hit Bonuses, and Melee Damage.  
When Attacking a larger Opponent, every Size category 
above Immense will give a +10 Bonus To Hit.  Unscalable allows the 
GM to make abstract rulings based on size. These should be 
considered set pieces more than structured fights or creatures. 
 When a Character is making an Attack against a Vehicle, 
they get a +5 Bonus To Hit for every two Size Points the Vehicle has.

PERCEPTIVE RANGE 
Perceptive Range is the Range that a Character is able to make Aim 
Actions and also reliably fire a weapon without Penalty. Perceptive 
Range is figured by multiplying the Character’s Perception 
Characteristic by 2. 
 Using Scopes, Sights, and Binoculars will multiply the 
Character’s Perceptive Range. 
 The Character will gain a -20 Penalty To Hit when making 
Attacks against Targets up to double their current Perceptive Range 
in Meters. 
 The Character will gain a -60 Penalty To Hit when making 
Attacks against Targets up to triple their current Perceptive Range in 
Meters. Any Attack beyond this will be impossible to hit. 
 You can find more on Perceptive Range in the Range 
Combat section of the book (p. 26). 
 
SOLDIER TYPES 
Soldier Types are your basic character building block based faction, 
race, and training. In Mythic, Soldier Types are categorized in factions 
of UNSC/Insurrectionist, Covenant/Banished, and Promethean. 
 A Soldier Type will give your Character’s Base 
Characteristics, Physical Attributes, Beginning Characteristic 
Advancements, Soldier Type Special Rules,  Equipment Packs, and 
more. (p. 50). 
 
EXPERIENCE (XP) 
Experience is used to increase Characteristics, gain new Skills and 
Abilities, and Educations. Characters will earn Experience for 
completing missions, roleplaying, finishing objectives, and defeating 
opponents. Experience is then spent  (p. 51) on various upgrades 
chosen by the Player between Missions or GM-chosen checkpoints.

9 
  
STARTING EXPERIENCE 
The GM will decide an amount of Experience the Players will begin 
with before the game starts. All Characters MUST begin with the same 
amount of Experience. This is important, as Soldier Types have an 
Experience Cost that must be spent to play as. This is what creates the 
balance between playing a Marine Character in a party that has 
Spartans or other stronger options. 
 
EXPERIENCE TIERS 
To help Players and GMs understand the strengths of different Soldier 
Types, each has been placed into an Experience Tier. These Tiers exist 
to help classify the differences of beginning strength between the 
various options in the game. The more powerful a Character is at 
Character Creation, the higher their Experience Cost and Experience 
Tier is. The Experience Tier Table can be found in Character Creation. 
 
CREDITS (CR) 
Credits, more commonly referred to as cR in 100DOS, is the main tool 
used to acquire Weapons, Armor, Equipment, and Vehicles. cR is 
mainly used to represent currency. However, the GM may use cR 
Acquisition, which is Military-based equipment acquisition. 
The GM will decide how much cR the Characters will begin 
with. Every Character should begin with the same amount unless the 
GM has a good reason to allow someone to begin with more. 
cR Payouts can be increased based on the Character’s Rank, 
which can be found in the Rank section of the Handbook (p. 399). 
 
CURRENCY CR 
Currency cR is the most common and simple use of cR.  With this, cR 
is treated as a currency that is earned and spent. The only limitations 
come from specific rules that can be found within the Armory section 
of the handbook.  
 
ACQUISITION CR 
Acquisition cR is an optional use of cR that shows how much the 
Character’s Faction is willing to allow them to use for their missions. 
Acquisition cR is a Military-themed use of cR that is earned the same 
way Currency cR is earned. However, the GM should limit the amount 
of equipment that can be taken onto the battlefield.  This is more for 
more military simulation style games. 
 Both Acquisition and Currency cR systems should be treated 
the exact same in terms of how much is earned . For example, a  
Marine and a Civilian should  each gain the same amount of cR, 
regardless of their Soldier Type. 
 
WEAPONS, ARMOR, AND EQUIPMENT 
Weapons, Armor, and Equipment are one of the most important 
aspect of your Character, both in Character Creation and later in the 
game. By spending cR, the Character will obtain various tools and 
resources they will use for any scenario imaginable. 100DOS’ 
Weapons, Armor, and Equipment sections of the book are extensive 
and cover almost all of your possible wants and needs, which can be 
found in the Armory section of the handbook (p. 107). 
 
SUPPORT POINTS (SP) 
Support P oints are given to Soldier Types that have military 
backgrounds, such as UNSC and Covenant forces. Support Points 
allow for a Character to call in three types of Support: Package, 
Backup, and Ordnance. More can be learned in the Support Point 
section of the handbook (p. 222). 
 
VEHICLES 
Vehicles are powerful pieces of equipment that can easily change the 
tide of battle. Vehicles are purchased with cR and cover a variety of 
vehicle types, from civilian to military, to walkers and flyers. (p. 232). 
LANGUAGES 
All Characters begin with one Language for free, which can be 
selected by the GM. Characters can learn up to their Intellect Modifier 
in Languages and each Language costs 150 Experience to learn.  The 
following is a list of example Languages. This list is incomplete and 
only serves as examples. *Program Language is any programming 
language of choice.

COMMUNICATION WITHOUT LANGUAGE 
A Character can attempt to communicate with another who does not 
know their Language. This involves using gestures, drawing, and using 
the environment to attempt to tell a simplistic story. To do so, the 
Character must make a -20 Charisma or Intellect Characteristic Test. 
For every Degree of Success on this Test, the other Character will gain 
a +5 on a -20 Investigation Skill Test.  If this Investigation Test is 
Successful, the other Character will understand the most simplistic 
version of what the Character is attempting to communicate. 
 
UPBRINGING, ENVIRONMENT, LIFESTYLES 
A Player is able to choose an Upbringing, Environment, and  3 
Lifestyles. These are character-building attributes given to Characters 
that offer small Bonuses and Penalties at Character Creation.  These 
can be found  here (p. 89). An option can’t be taken if the 
Characteristic would be lowered to 5 or below. 
The Character’s Upbringing represents how the Character 
was raised and will give a set of Environments that can be taken. 
The Character’s Environment will show where they spent 
the majority of their life, helping mold them. 
The Character’s Lifestyles show what the Character did to 
shape them into the person they are today. 
 
SKILLS 
Skills are the representation of the Character’s training and 
understanding in various trades. They allow a Character to interact 
with, or improve their interactions with various aspects of the 
100DOS game system.  Further explanation of Skills and all types of 
Skills can be found here (p. 89). 
 
ABILITIES 
Abilities are proficiencies and talents a Character can learn that 
improve their chances of survival in both combat and social scenarios. 
Abilities are gained by spending Experience and meeting the 
necessary Prerequisites. Abilities and their explanations can be found 
in the Abilities section of the handbook (p. 97). 
 
EDUCATIONS 
Educations are a supplemental utilit y a Character can learn to 
enhance both Characteristic and Skill Tests.  These are a Character’s 
extensive knowledge and understanding of subjects, which can be 
used on tests based on the scenario.  Educations come in two types, 
Education and Street Smarts. Educations can be found here (p. 105).

ACTIONS 
 
WHAT ARE ACTIONS 
Actions are types of opportunities a Character may take advantage of 
or activities they can make during their Turn. Each Turn has two Half 
Actions, or a Full Action in total, they are able to make each Round. 
Actions are split into two major Categories: Combat and Non-Combat. 
 
USING ACTIONS 
During a character’s turn, the character may perform one Full Action 
or two Half Actions. A character could, for example, make a Readied 
Stance for their turn (Full Action), or Ready an Explosive and use it 
(Two Half Actions). It is important to remember that a single Round is 
only six seconds in length, so a character can only do so much. 
 Most actions are started and completed within the active 
character’s same turn. If not, these are known as Extended Actions.  
 
FULL ACTIONS 
A Full Action requires the character’s full turn to accomplish. A 
Character is able to make a Full Action for their Turn, leaving them 
unable to take any other Action. 
 
HALF ACTIONS 
Half Actions are simple and only require some effort. It consumes 
roughly half of the turn’s time that can the character. A character can 
take two Half Actions on their turn. Some Half Actions can happen at 
the same time, such as readying two weapons, allowing the character 
to take their next Half Action as an attack. 
 
STACKING ACTIONS 
There are instances where multiple Actions can be taken at once, such 
as moving and firing a weapon. For example, if the Character were to 
take a Full Action to Run, that Character could also take a Half Action 
to fire their weapon  during this Run Action.  Many times, Stacking 
Actions like these will come with Penalties. 
 
REACTION 
A Reaction is a type of Action that is used to react or counter to an 
Action that is targeting the Character. These do not take up the 
Character’s Half or Full Actions and may be used as many times as 
possible based on the Penalties Reactions gain.  Reactions can’t be 
Stacked with other Actions or Reactions. 
Reactions are used for various Actions such as Evading 
Attacks, using Physical Shields multiple times, or attempting to catch 
an object.  
 Each time a Reaction is made, any Reaction afterwards is at 
a stacking -10 Penalty. These Penalties are removed at the beginning 
of the Character’s next Turn. 
 
FREE ACTIONS 
A Free Action takes only a snap of the finger to use and requires little 
to no effort to complete. Free Actions may be performed in addition 
to any other Actions made in any characters’ turn. The GM should use 
common sense to set a reasonable limit for the  Turn. Free Actions 
include dropping an item or speaking 6 seconds worth of dialogue. 
 
ACTION SUBTYPES 
Action Subtypes help categorize the Action being used. Movement is 
for when a Character moves, Attack is used for Attacks  made, and 
Concentration is for when Characters need to focus on the Action. 
 
COMBINED ACTIONS 
Combined Actions allow Characters to do more precise Actions in 
groups of two or more. When Characters opt into a Combined Action, 
they go at the lowest Initiative in the participating group. This Action 
must be declared during the Turn of the highest initiative in the group. 
Characters with higher Initiatives must then wait to take their Turn 
with the slower Characters. 
 
EXTENDED ACTIONS 
Extended Actions are Actions that need longer than a Full Action to 
perform. Extended Actions will list how long they take to perform by 
either listing a set amount of Half Actions, Full Actions, or Turns. 
 
SPEAKING ACTIONS 
Speaking Actions are Free Actions that can be expressed within 6 
seconds, fitting into the Character’s Turn. It is left to the GM to decide 
what a player might be able to say in that amount of time. An insult 
to an enemy or a quick order to attack someone is reasonable, but 
anything that goes into detail or takes longer than six seconds to say 
counts as taking an Extended Action. 
 
 
COMBAT ACTIONS 
 
ACTION LENGTH SUBTYPE DESCRIPTION 
Aim Half/Full Concentration Aiming action to use with weapons. 
Blind Fire Half/Full Attack Firing around cover without revealing yourself to the enemy. 
Brace Weapon Half/Full Misc. Preparation to use a weapon with the Heavy Weapon Trait.

AIM ACTION 
LENGTH: Half or Full Action SUBTYPE: Concentration 
The active Character takes extra time to make sure their attack is 
precise. Aiming is a Half or Full Action at base but may be considered 
Extended if stated otherwise. This is used with both Warfare Melee 
and Warfare Range Characteristics. 
 Aiming as a Half Action gives the Character a +5 To  Hit to 
the first Attack Roll made during the Character’s Turn. Aiming as a Full 
Action will give a +10 To Hit for the first two Attack Rolls made. 
An Aim Action will last until the Character moves f arther 
than their Half Move during their Turn, takes damage, or the Target 
moves more than the Character’s Perception Modifier in Meters in a 
single Round. Aim Actions will also be lost if the Character switches 
weapons, scopes, or uses a Reaction. 
If the Character took a Half Action Aim, they may later 
spend a second Half Action to gain the benefits of the Full Action Aim. 
Aim Actions can’t be taken if the Target is farther than their 
Perceptive Range (p. 26). 
If a Melee Attack that had an Aim Action deals Special 
Damage, the Special Damage is increased by the Character’s 
Perception Modifier multiplied by 5. 
 
CALLED SHOT 
LENGTH: Half Action of Attacks SUBTYPE: Concentration Attack 
Called Shots are when a Character attempts to call out specific body 
parts to Attack.  
Attacking a specific body location gives the Character a -30 
Penalty To Hit, while attacking a sublocation gives a -60 Penalty To 
Hit. If the roll is successful, the shot is made and hits the chosen 
location. 
 Called Shot effects a Half Action worth of Attacks each time 
it is used, and the Locations targeted can’t be changed within these 
Half Actions. The Character may change targeted locations with each 
Half Action taken.  
Called Shots taken against weaponry are possible. Standard 
weaponry come at a -40 Penalty, while attacks against Large and 
Heavy weapons come at a -20 Penalty. 
If the Called Shot missed, but still would have hit with 2 
Degrees of Success as a standard Attack (without a Called Shot), it will 
still hit the target. The Called Shot is ignored and the To Hit roll will be 
made to see which Location is struck. 
 
BLIND FIRE 
LENGTH: Half or Full Action SUBTYPE: Attack 
Characters can fire around corners, above cover, or fire their weapon 
without seeing the target, if they know the general location. 
When using Blind Fire, shots are made at a -60 Penalty. 
Blind Fire gains no Bonuses from Aiming Actions or from any To  Hit 
Bonuses gained from Equipment like sights, scopes, and lasers. 
 When using Smartlink devices, the Blind Fire Penalty is 
reduced to -30 and the Character may gain Bonuses from Aiming 
Actions and Targeting Lasers. 
 Blind Fire may be used alongside Suppressing Fire . This 
removes the 10% chance to strike Targets and all Penalties it causes 
Opponents will be halved. 
 Blind Fire may be used against Cloaked and Camouflaged 
Characters. While attempting to use Blind Fire to Attack a Character, 
they still gain the -60 Penalty but can’t reduce it -30 unless they also 
have VISR or any other Equipment that assists in spotting Camouflage 
and Cloaked Characters. 
  
EVADE 
See the Evasion Skill on (p. 93) 
BRACE WEAPON 
LENGTH: Half Action SUBTYPE: Misc. 
Bracing is a Half Action needed to use [HW] Heavy Weapons without 
Penalty, as well as removing the Penalties given by the Long Barrel 
Special Rule. Bracing will also halve the Penalties and Drop Chance 
when firing weapons One-Handed and Dual-Wielding. 
 When use a [HW] Heavy Weapon while it isn’t Braced, all 
Attacks made with it will gain a -20 Penalty. At the end of each To Hit 
Test, a Strength Test must be made. If failed, the Character drops the 
weapon and no further Attacks can be made with the weapon until it 
is picked up again. 
 Characters are able to move up to their Half Action in 
Meters per Turn and still be considered Braced. If the Character 
moves any further in a single Turn, the y are no longer considered 
Braced. This means that in a Half Action, the Character can move up 
to half of their Half Move. 
 
CHARGE ATTACK 
LENGTH: Full Action SUBTYPE: Attack, Movement 
The target must be at least the Character’s Full Move away in Meters 
and no further than the Character’s Charge Movement Speed in 
Meters (p. 15). When Charging, the Character moves in a straight line 
and may make one of the following actions: 
Attack: Make a single Melee Attack  with a +10 Bonus. The 
Charge Attack increases the Pierce of the Attack equal to the Meters 
traveled in the Charge. 
Tackle: The Character attempts to knock their Opponent 
Prone on the ground with a Successful Opposed Strength, Agility, or 
Warfare Melee Test. The Attacking Character gains a +5 Bonus to this 
Opposed Test for every 10 meters the Character traveled during the 
Charge Action, to a maximum of +30. 
The Tackle will deal half of the Damage that a Charge Attack 
would have dealt, but places the Character in control of a Grapple, 
which can be left as a Free Action with no Penalties or Tests needed 
from the Attacking Character. 
  
FORCED REPOSITION 
LENGTH: Half Action SUBTYPE: Attack, Movement 
When using Forced Reposition, the Active Character attempts to force 
the opponent a number of meters equal to half their Half Move. This 
is done through an Opposed Warfare Melee and is treated as a 
Grapple. If the Active Character wins, the opposing character is 
moved in the direction the Active Character is attempting to go. If the 
opponent succeeds, they go nowhere. 
 
GRAPPLE 
LENGTH: Half or Full Action SUBTYPE: Attack 
The Character defends or attacks a Grapple Action, which are Actions 
listed under the Grapple section of Melee Combat. These Actions can 
be initiating a Grapple, attempting to Break a Grapple, or any Action 
made during a Grapple Action.  Grappling also covers Holds and 
Throws, each with their own options and transitions. The Grapple 
options can be found in the Grapple section of Melee Combat (p. 33). 
 
GUARDED ATTACK 
LENGTH: Half Action SUBTYPE: Concentration Attack 
The character performs a carefully made attack to keep a more 
defensive stance. When making a Guarded Attack, the character 
suffers a -10 Penalty to Warfare Melee and Range Tests but gain a +10 
Bonus to all Evasion tests until the beginning of the character’s next 
turn. Any Bonuses and Penalties gained from a Guarded Attack is lost 
if the character has been knocked down or stunned.

===== PAGE 12 =====
12 
  
KILLZONE 
LENGTH: Full Action SUBTYPE: Concentration 
A Killzone is a 45 -degree cone facing a chosen direction , which is 
made as a Combined Action with any amount of Characters wanting 
to join in. Each Character holds their Action when joining a Killzone, 
which will be used to ambush anyone who walks into the Killzone. 
 The Killzone ’s Range is the highest Perceptive Range of 
those in the Combined Action, in meters, not accounting for anything 
that extends Perceptive Range. Only the Characters using a Scope will 
gain the Killzone’s benefits up to that range. 
 When a Target walks into or begins their Turn in a Killzone 
will have their Turn interrupted by those in the Killzone.  The Target 
can then take their Turn after all Characters involved in the Killzone 
make their Attack. This is done by the Attacking Characters taking 
their held Turn. 
This can only happen if the Killzone was set up the previous 
Round, or earlier. If an Opponent enters the Killzone within the same 
Round, they will not have their Turn interrupted and the Killzone will 
only be able to be used at the beginning of the lowest Initiative 
Character’s Turn. 
 Opponents who move into the Killzone take double the 
Penalties from Suppressing Fire. 
 The direction of the Killzone may be changed once per Turn, 
but the Opponent will not gain extra Penalties from Suppressing Fire 
if they enter the Killzone within the same Round as the change. 
 
READIED STANCE 
LENGTH: Half Action SUBTYPE: Concentration Attack 
The Active Character concentrates entirely on self-defense, taking no 
Actions beyond speech. The Active Character using Readied Stance 
may make two Reactions that gives no Penalties, such as a Snapshot 
giving a -20 Penalty to the next Reaction, or an Evasi on giving a -10 
Penalty to the next Reaction. 
 
RELOAD 
LENGTH: Varies SUBTYPE: Misc. 
The Character reloads a weapon that takes ammunition. The length 
of the Reload Action depends on the Weapon being reloaded, which 
is listed as the Weapon’s “Reload” or “Reload Time.” 
 Weapons have base Reload Times depending on the 
Weapon Type . These are the Half Actions needed to reload the 
weapon. A Weapon’s base Reload Time is reduced by 1 for every 2 
Modifiers in both the Agility and Warfare Range Characteristics 
separately, to a minimum of 1. 
 
RELOADING UNKNOWN WEAPONS: 
When reloading a weapon that the Character doesn’t have the 
Faction Training for, the weapon will reload at 3x the Reload Time. 
Once the Character has successfully reloaded the weapon or was 
shown how to reload the weapon, they will be able to reload it at only 
2x the Reload Time. Once the Character has the Faction Training, the 
extended reload time is removed. 
 
SINGLE LOADING WEAPONS: 
Single Loading is needed for Weapons that list having Single Loading 
under the Reload, or when attempting to load Magazines and Belts in 
Structured Time. A Character can load 1 shell or round for every 2 
modifiers in Agility and Warfare Range Characteristics, to a maximum 
of 4 per Half Action. 
 
BELT-FED WEAPON RELOADING ASSISTANCE: 
Belt-Fed weapons take time to reload and can be assisted by a second 
Character to speed up the process. This halves the base Reload Time 
of the weapon. The weapon does not gain the benefits of the assisting 
Character’s Warfare Range and Agility Characteristics. 
 
STANDARD ATTACK 
LENGTH: Half or Full Action SUBTYPE: Attack 
The Active Character makes a Ranged or Melee Attack as a Half or Full 
Action. The number of Attacks is dictated by the weapon being used. 
For example, if a Rifle has Semi-Auto (3), the Character may make up 
to 3 Attacks in a Half Action, or 6 Attacks as a Full Action. 
 If the attacking character is unarmed, the character can still 
attempt to make an Unarmed Attack, Grapple, or Hold. 
 Ranged Attack options and rules can be found in the Ranged 
Attack section of the handbook (p. 26). 
 Melee Attack options and rules can be found in the Melee 
Attack section of the handbook (p. 29). 
 
SUPPRESSING FIRE 
LENGTH: Full Action SUBTYPE: Attack 
Suppressing Fire is where a Character, or a Group using a Combined 
Action, fires wildly at an Opponent to force them to stay in Cover.  
 Suppressing Fire effects out to 5 Meters from the Target, 
and in front of and behind the Target. The effect will only pass 
through walls if it pierces through.  When using Suppressing Fire, the 
Character will fire the maximum amount of ammunition in a Full 
Action that the Weapon can handle. 
 Characters under Suppressing Fire must make a -(X) 
Courage Test or be Pinned, where (X) is 10 for each Character in the 
Suppressing Fire Action. (X) is increased by 20 for each Heavy Weapon 
firing or any weapon firing more than 6 shots in a Turn. Dual Wielding 
weapons will count as a single weapon being fired and both rate of 
fire of the weapons are added together. Pinned Characters may redo 
the Courage Test at the beginning of their Turn to no longer be 
Pinned. For each Round failed, they gain a stacking +10 Bonus for the 
next attempt.  
 Pinned Characters can only stay in Cover and take Actions 
that would keep them safe or alive. Pinned Characters are at a +10 To 
Hit by flanking Characters. 
 Characters who stand up or enter Suppressing Fire have a 
10% chance per Weapon being fired to be struck. The GM may roll or 
decide which of the weapons involved strikes the Character. 
 
TACTICAL ADVANCE 
LENGTH: Full Action SUBTYPE: Movement 
The Active Character moves from one point of cover to the next. In 
doing so, the character may cover a distance up to their Full Action 
move. For the duration of the move, the character is considered to 
benefit from the cover the character left from, even though the 
character is moving for a moment.  All Attack Actions made during a 
Tactical Advance suffer an additional -10 Penalty To Hit. 
 
THROWING OBJECTS 
LENGTH: Half or Full Action SUBTYPE: Attack, Misc. 
As a Half Action, the Character will throw an object that was readied 
in their hand. This can cover throwing Grenades, improvised 
weapons, and throwing weapons. 
 Unless specified otherwise, throwing an object single -
handed is a Half Action, and throwing an object with two hands is a 
Full Action. 
 When throwing objects, damage and distance thrown can 
be found here (p. 36).

===== PAGE 13 =====
13 
  
NON-COMBAT ACTIONS 
ACTION LENGTH SUBTYPE DESCRIPTION 
Crouch, Stand, Prone Varies Movement Prone to Crouch, or Crouch to Stand 
Delay Action Full Misc. Before your next Turn, take any Half Action. 
Haggle Varies Concentration, Social Effort to lower prices or reduce trades and negotiations.  
Jump or Leap Half/Full Movement Jump vertically or horizontally. If movement is 10+ meters, takes Full Action. 
Lock Picking Varies Concentration Using the Security Skill to attempt removing physical locks. 
Move Varies Movement Making a Move Action based on different Movement types. 
Performance Varies Concentration, Social Performing various entertainment-oriented actions. Varies in time. 
Ready Half Misc. Ready a weapon or item. 
Sleight of Hand Half/Full Concentration Attempting to trick or steal from others with the use of their hands. 
Mount Half Movement Begin mounting a target. 
Use a Skill Varies Concentration, misc. Use of a skill. 
 
CROUCH, STAND, AND PRONE 
LENGTH: Free or Half Action SUBTYPE: Movement 
Standing to a Crouch or standing from a Crouch is a Free Action, once 
per Turn. Any other Crouch or Standing movement takes a Half Action 
to perform, instead. 
While Prone a character may only make Half  or Full Move 
Actions at half of their Movement Speeds. 
A Character can go from Standing and Crouching to Prone 
as either a Free Action Dive or as a Half Action Drop. Diving will cause 
all other Actions during the Turn to be at a -30 Penalty but will also 
give Opponents targeting them a -30 Penalty To Hit until the 
beginning of the Character’s next Turn.  
A Character who took a Dive Action can’t Crouch or Stand 
until the beginning of their next Turn. The Character may also Dive up 
to their Half Move if Standing, or half of their Half Move if Diving while 
Crouching. 
If the Character was taking a Charge or Run Action that was 
uninterrupted during their previous Turn, they may make a Running 
Dive. A Running Dive is a Free Action that lets the Character move up 
to their Full Move in Meters. 
The Character can take a Half Action to Drop to Prone 
without Penalty, but no other Actions can be taken while Dropping.  
Going from Prone to Standing or Crouching is a Half Action. 
Movement options while Crouching and Prone can be 
found in the Movement Section (p. 15) of the handbook. 
 
DELAY 
LENGTH: Full Action SUBTYPE: Misc. 
Instead of acting immediately, the character waits for an opportunity 
they can act upon. When a character chooses Delay, the character’s 
turn “ends,” and any time before the start of the character’s next 
turn, the character can take one Half Action. If the Character attempts 
to interrupt another Character’s Action, an Opposed Agility Test must 
be made by both. The Character who wins the Opposed Test will be 
able to act first.  
If two or more characters take a Delayed Action, they must 
make an opposed Agility Test to see who acts first. 
 
HAGGLE 
LENGTH: Varies SUBTYPE: Concentration, Social 
When attempting to haggle prices, a Character must roleplay out a 
scenario. The better the reasoning, the higher the modifiers should 
be for that Character.  
 When attempting to Haggle, the Characters must use their 
Negotiation Skill. For every Degree of Success above the seller the 
buyer gets, the price drops, to a maximum of 4 Degrees of Success.  
 Gaining Degrees of Failure has a chance to reduce that 
Character’s Disposition towards the Character attempting to Haggle 
but will not increase the price. 
DEGREES OF SUCCESS MODIFIER 
0 5% Discount 
1 10% Discount 
2 15% Discount 
3 20% Discount 
4 25% Discount 
 
JUMP OR LEAP 
LENGTH: Full Action SUBTYPE: Movement 
Characters can Jump vertically or Leap horizontally. See Movement 
for details on Jumping and Leaping. 
Movement options for Jumping and Leaping can be found 
in the Movement Section (p. 16) of the handbook. 
 
LOCK PICKING 
LENGTH: Varies SUBTYPE: Concentration 
When figuring how to pick a lock, the GM assigns a Lock a difficulty 
Value, from 1 being easy, to 15 for incredibly difficult. Every Full 
Action, the Character must attempt to gain that many Degrees of 
Success in an Extended Action using their Security Ski ll (p. 89). Every 
Degree of Success gives a point towards the goal, while every Degree 
of Failure removes one point. Once the difficult value is reached, the 
lock is disarmed. Every Test made to reach the needed goal is a Full 
Action. Locks that are Difficulty 10 and over will reset Degrees of 
Success and Degrees of Failure if the Extended Action is stopped 
without the lock being disarmed.  
 
MOUNT 
LENGTH: Half Action SUBTYPE: Movement 
If the character is already standing, the character may begin a 
mounting action to ride a beast or vehicle  or begin climbing a 
character at least two sizes larger. 
 
MOVE 
LENGTH: Half or Full Action SUBTYPE: Movement 
The Active Character can choose to make multiple types of Movement 
Actions found within the book. Half Action Move, Full Action Move, 
Charge, Run, and Sprint (p. 15). This can also cover Swim and Climb 
Actions, as well as Falling, special movement in Gravity, and more. 
While moving, a Character is still able to make other Actions 
that do not involve other movement types simultaneously. These 
come with Penalties to performing the Actions, such as making a 
Ranged Attack, or a Skill Test.  
Melee Attacks can be made during a Movement Action but 
only a single Melee Attack can be made against a Character they are 
passing by during their Move. You are still limited to the amount of 
Melee Attacks you can make per Turn, regardless of how many people 
you are passing by. 
The Movement and other Actions taken can’t surpass a Full 
Action.

===== PAGE 14 =====
14 
  
PERFORMANCE 
LENGTH: Varies SUBTYPE: Concentration, Social 
Musical performance is an Action that allows a Character to dance, 
play musical instruments, sing, and play out acts. Each type of 
performance has a modifier that alters the difficulty of the Action 
being made. 
 A Performance Action uses the Appeal or Stunting Skill, 
depending on how the Character is attempting to go about their 
Action. The GM and Player may work together to decide how they 
perform their Action. The Acting Performance may be used with the 
Deception Skill, instead of Appeal or Stunting. 
 The amount of Degrees of Success the Performance Test 
made the better the performance’s outcome. For every two Degrees 
of Success made on the Test, the GM may improve the Disposition of 
an NPC. 
 
PERFORMANCE MODIFIER 
Acting -10 
Dancing -10 
Difficult Dance -40 
Intricate Dance -30 
Musical Instrument with Education -- 
Musical Instrument without Education -30 
Singing -- 
 
READY 
LENGTH: Half Action SUBTYPE: Misc. 
Ready is when an Active Character draws a weapon or retrieves an 
object that was stowed away or holstered. Skills and Talents may 
affect the speed at which items are readied, such as Quickdraw. This 
can be used to apply poisons or to administer a drug. 
 
SLEIGHT OF HAND 
LENGTH: Half or Full Action SUBTYPE: Concentration 
Sleight of Hand is an Action that involves a Character being 
backhanded or sneaky with actions performed with their hands. 
Sleight of Hand includes actions like Pickpocketing, manipulating 
items so that no one will notice, or even magic tricks like making a 
coin disappear. Sleight of Hand Actions have modifiers that alter the 
difficulty of the action being taken. Underneath this is a table that 
offers examples of Sleight of Hand Actions. 
 Sleight of Hand involves actions such as attempting to steal 
from the pocket or pouch of another Character, otherwise known as 
Pickpocketing. A pickpocket is generally done by trying to remove 
small items from a pouch or source worn by a Character without them 
noticing.  
 Sleight of Hand uses the Deception Skill as its base and is 
opposed by the Opponent’s Investigation Skill. 
 A failed Sleight of Hand Action will alert the Character the 
Action is against. If the Opponent wins the Opposed Test, they are 
aware of the Actions made by the Character. 
 
SLEIGHT OF HAND MODIFIER 
Magic Trick +10 
Card Trick -- 
Pickpocket an ID Card -10 
Pickpocket a concealed handgun -40 
Hide or draw out a small weapon or object -10 
Hide or draw out a medium-size weapon or object -20 
Remove a weapon from its sheath -30 
Hide or draw out a large weapon or object -40 
 
SKILL USE 
LENGTH: Varies SUBTYPE: Concentration, Misc. 
The Active Character may use a skill. This involves making a Skill Test. 
The time in which the Skill test takes place is determined by the skill 
being used. The Skill section can be found here (p. 89).  
 
VEHICLE USE 
This table shows the Actions using a Vehicle will take. For further 
explanation on these Actions, see the Vehicle Section of the 
handbook (p. 232). 
 
ACTION LENGTH 
Accelerate and Brake Full Action 
Maneuver Reaction 
Weapon Use Weapon-specified 
Vehicle Modification or System Half Action 
 
ACTIONS NOT COVERED 
If a character wants to do an action not covered by the game rules, 
the GM should attempt to allow the action. The GM should consider 
whichever Skill or Characteristic the Action could cover. The GM and 
Players should write down how they handled the Action for later use.

MOVEMENT 
 
The Movement section show s how fast Characters can move, how 
they can climb, swim, jump, and so on. 
 During Combat Rounds, the Character may take specified 
Movement Actions which can be found under the Non -Combat 
Actions section of the book. The table below gives a quick reference 
to these Movement Actions in Meters. The Movement Actions can go 
beyond an Agility Modifier of 9, these are just examples. 
 
MOD HALF FULL CHARGE RUN SPRINT

CROUCHING AND PRONE MOVEMENT 
Standing to a Crouch or standing from a Crouch is a Free Action, once 
per Turn. Any other Crouch or Standing movement takes a Half Action 
to perform, instead. 
While Prone a character may only make Half  or Full Move 
Actions at half of their Movement Speeds. 
 
CROUCHING AND PRONE IN COMBAT 
While Crouching, a Character is at a -5 to be hit by Ranged Attacks, 
but at a +5 to be hit by Melee Attacks. While Prone, a Character is at 
a -10 to be hit by Ranged Attacks, but at a +10 to be hit by Melee 
Attacks. 
 
DIFFICULT AND DANGEROUS TERRAIN 
Difficult and Dangerous Terrain reduce Movement and impose  
Penalties on Climbing, Swimming, Agility, and Warfare Characteristic 
Tests. Difficult and Dangerous Terrain reduce Movement in both 
Narrative and Structured Time. 
 Characters moving through Difficult Terrain can’t use their 
Run or Sprint Movement Actions. The Character can’t Hurry or Run in 
Narrative Time. 
 Characters moving through Dangerous Terrain can only 
move their Half Move as a Full Action. This reduces the amount of the 
Character’s Narrative Movement by 50% and can’t Hurry or Run in 
Narrative Time. 
 The following are examples of Penalties given towards 
Athletics and Piloting Skill Tests, and any Movement -based Agility 
Characteristic Tests for Difficult and Dangerous Terrain. 
 
CONDITIONS PENALTY TO TESTS TYPE 
Heavy Fog or Smoke -10 if Hurrying or Running Difficult 
Darkness, Dense Crowds -20 if Hurrying or Running Difficult 
Rubble, Sand -10 Difficult 
Ice, Mud -20 Difficult 
Craters, Mountain Side -30 Dangerous 
Unstable Ground -30 Dangerous 
Thin Ice -40 Dangerous 
Large Earthquakes -50 Dangerous 
 
HALF MOVE 
Half Moving takes a Half Action to perform. A Character may perform 
another non-movement Half Action simultaneously at a -20 Penalty.  
 Two Half Moves may be taken per Turn, this turns the Half 
Move into a Full Move. 
 
FULL MOVE 
A Full Move takes a Full Action to perform. A Character may perform 
another non -movement Half or full Action simultaneously at a -20 
Penalty. 
 
CHARGE 
A Charge takes a Full Action to perform. A Character may perform a 
non-Movement and non-Melee Half Action simultaneously at a -30 
Penalty. The Charge Movement can be finished with a special Melee 
Attack. More information on this Charge Attack Action can be found 
in the Combat Actions section (p. 10). 
 
RUN 
A Run takes a Full Action to perform. A Character may perform a non-
movement Half Action simultaneously at a -40 Penalty. 
 
SPRINT 
The Sprint Action takes a Full Action to perform. A character can’t 
perform another Action simultaneously.  A Sprint Action can only be 
taken using the Blur Ability. (p. 97). 
 
MOVEMENT ACTIONS AND POSSIBLE ATTACKS 
When a Character is making Movement Actions and attempting to 
strike a Target, the GM must decide whether that Character is able to 
see or strike the Target for the duration of the movement. If the GM 
decides that the Target was not visible during part of the Movement, 
the GM may decide how many of their Attacks the Character can end 
up making successfully. 
 
NARRATIVE MOVEMENT TABLE 
Narrative Movement assumes that a Character is walking at a normal 
pace using their Full Move. This does not include obstacles, Difficult, 
or Dangerous Terrain. 
 Narrative Movement is based on the Character’s Agility 
Modifier, and the multiplier needed to multiply to their Agility Mod is 
listed at the bottom. 
 Characters carrying 50% to 75% of their Carry Weight 
reduce their Agility Mod by 1 , to a minimum of 0. Carrying 76% to 
100% of their Carry Weight will reduce their Agility Mod by 2, instead.
 Travel assumes the Character spends 10 minutes resting per 
hour moved. Distance traveled per day assumes 15 hours of 
uninterrupted moment. 
 
AGILITY MOD PER MINUTE PER HOUR PER DAY

9 180 m 9 km 135 km

HURRYING AND NARRATIVE TIME 
A Character is able to Hurry in Narrative Time , traveling at their 
Charge Movement Speed instead of their Full Move. To do this, the 
Character takes the Per Minute, Hour, and Day values and multiply 
them by 2. The Character can perform this for 2 hours per Toughness 
Modifier. Every hour after gives a level of Fatigue. 
 
RUNNING AND NARRATIVE TIME 
A Character is able to Run in Narrative Time , traveling at their Run 
Movement Speed instead of their Full Move. To do this, the Character 
takes the Per Minute, Hour, and Day values and multiply them by 3. 
The Character can perform this for 10 minutes per Toughness 
Modifier. Every 10 minutes after gives a level of Fatigue. 
 
CLIMBING 
There may be times where a character needs to climb over a wall but 
does not have the ability of flight. Climbing is divided into two types, 
Simple and Difficult. 
There are times where a Climb Test will be requested from 
the Player or GM. A Climb Test is where the Character must make an 
Athletics or Stunting Test in order to make progress while climbing.  
A Character can Climb up to their Half Move in Meters as a 
Full Action. A Character attempting to hurry a Climb can move up to 
their Full Action Move in Meters as a Full Action but must make a 
Climb Test to be able to successfully pull this off. This is known as the 
Character’s Climb Speed. 
 
SIMPLE CLIMBS 
Simple Climbs include fences, walls, craters, or anything else that 
requires simple effort to move over. Any character with both hands 
free can easily accomplish Simple Climbs without a needed Test, just 
the time needed to perform them.  
 If a Character is trying to climb quickly , or climb while 
holding objects with their hands, they must make a -10 Climbing Test. 
If Failed, the Character can’t make it any higher, if Failed with two or 
more Degrees of Failure, the Character falls. 
 
DIFFICULT CLIMBS 
Difficult Climbs are beyond the means of an ordinary climb. A Cliff 
with overheads, buildings with no handholds, and icy precipices are 
examples of Difficult Climbs. Difficult Climbs must have a Climb Test. 
 A Character may make as many attempts as needed to 
perform a Climb Test, while the GM is expected to apply a Difficulty 
Modifier based on how difficult they want the climb to be.  If 
Successful, the Character begins making progress based on their 
Climb Speed. 
 Characters should gain large Bonuses (Such as +40) to the 
Test for using intelligent ways up, such as abseiling and harnessing. A 
character can descend and ascend Difficult Climbs more quickly by 
abseiling and harnessing, using chains and climbing gear to traverse 
the climbs. This doubles the Character’s Climb Speed. 
 
JUMPING AND LEAPING DISTANCES 
 A jump is a controlled vertical ascent or descent where the character 
either jumps as high as they can or jumps down safely. A Leap is where 
the Character is jumping for distance, instead of height.  Performing 
any kind of Jump or Leap is treated as Half Action unless the character 
is jumping or leaping farther than 10 Meters. A Jump will last a Half 
Action for every 10 Meters traveled. 
 A character’s jump height is a fourth (1/4th) of their Strength 
Modifier in meters. A character’s Leap distance is the highest of their 
Half Agility Modifier, or Half Strength Modifier. A running start for a 
jump is able to increase this distance by +1 Meter for every 10 Meters 
they are traveling during their Turn. 
SWIMMING 
There may be times where a Character needs to swim across bodies 
of water or to stay afloat. Swimming is divided into two types, Simple 
and Difficult. 
 There are times where a Swimming Test will be requested 
from the Player or GM. A Swimming Test is where the Characte r 
makes a Strength or Agility Test. 
 A Character can Swim up to their Strength Modifier in 
Meters per Turn, not including Mythic Strength . This is known as 
Swimming Speed. 
 
SIMPLE SWIMMING 
Simple Swimming  includes calm waters, short depths, or assisted 
swimming using a device. Any Character with both hands free can 
easily accomplish Simple Swimming without a needed Test, just the 
time needed to perform the Test. 
 If a Character is trying to swim quickly or swim while holding 
an object that doesn’t assist in floating, they must make a -10 
Swimming Test. If Failed , the Character’s Swim Speed is halved. If 
Failed with two or more Degrees of Failure, the Character gains no 
distance. 
 
DIFFICULT SWIMMING 
Difficult Swimming goes beyond the means of ordinary means of 
swimming. Fast -moving water, underto w, rapids, swimming with 
heavy weights, and swimming during combat are all examples. 
 A Character may make as many attempts as needed to 
perform a Swim Test, while the G M is expected to apply a Difficulty 
Modifier based on how difficult the Swim needs to be. If Successful, 
the Character begins making progress based on their Swimming 
Speed. If the GM decides, Swimming Speed can be reduce d. This can 
be caused by undertows, rapids, and fast-moving water. 
 Characters should gain large Bonuses (such as +40) to the 
Test for using intelligent ways to swim, such as using flotation devices 
or ropes to guide their way across.  This doubles the Character’s 
Swimming Speed. 
 
SWIMMING WITH WEIGHT 
If the Character has more than 50% of their Carry Weight, Swimming 
Tests are at a -10 Penalty and Swimming Speed is reduced by 1.  
If the Character has more than 75% of their Carry Weight, 
Swimming Tests are at a -30 Penalty and Swimming Speed is reduced 
by 2. 
If the Character is at 90% or higher, all Swimming Tests are 
at a -50 Penalty and Swimming Speed is reduced by 3.  
If the Character is over-encumbered, the Character can’t 
make Swimming Tests without a flotation device of some kind to 
assist them to swim. If the Character’s Swimming Speed is reduced to 
or below 0, they can’t make progress swimming. 
 
UNDERWATER 
A Character can choose to swim underwater for both Simple and 
Difficult Swimming. The Character’s Swimming Speed is not affected  
by being underwater. Underwater Characters gain a +20 Bonus to 
Camouflage. When underwater, the Character must hold their 
breath. To find out how long a Character is capable of holding their 
breath, check the Holding Breath entry under the Medical Effects  
section of the handbook. 
 If a Character failed to swim, they are considered going 
underwater for their Turn. If the Character has failed twice in a row 
to swim, their Swimming Tests will be at a -20 Penalty until successful.

===== PAGE 17 =====
17 
  
SWIMMING IN NARRATIVE TIME 
Extended Swimming can be exhausting. A character can swim for a 
number of hours equal to the character’s Toughness Mod. After this 
point, the character must make a Toughness Test per hour with a 
cumulative -10 Penalty per each hour. On a failed test, the character 
takes +1 level of Fatigue for every Degree of Failure. If the character 
falls unconscious due to Fatigue, the character goes underwater. If 
the character needs to breathe, the character begins to Suffocate. 
 
FIGURING CARRY WEIGHTS 
Carry Weight is how much a Character can hold while still moving 
normally with no issues or slowdown. This is figured by adding half of 
the Character’s Strength and Toughness Characteristics together. For 
example, a Strength of 45 and a Toughness of 50 means a Carry 
Weight of 95  divided by 2, becoming 47 Kilograms. Mythic Strength 
and Toughness will each increase their respective Characteristic by 10 
when figuring Carry Weight. Traveling with more than Carry Weight is 
called being Over-Encumbered, which is found below. 
 
LIFT WEIGHT 
To figure Lift Weight, you multiply the Carry Weight by 3. A 
Character’s Lift Weight is the weight they can safely Lift something 
without overexerting themselves.   
If the weight being lifted reaches the Character’s Push 
Weight or the Character can no longer move, the Character gains a 
Degree of Fatigue and can’t move any further until weight is dropped. 
 
PUSH WEIGHT 
To Figure Push Weight, you multiply the Carry Weight by 5. This is the 
weight a Character can push or pull objects. 
 When attempting to surpass the Push Weight, up to 6x the 
Carry Weight , the Character must make a Strength Test. For every 
Degree of Failure, they take a Degree of Fatigue. 
 
OVER-ENCUMBERED CHARACTERS 
If a character attempts to overexert himself by Carrying Weight, they 
are Over-Encumbered. An Over -Encumbered Character gains a -20 
Penalty on any Tests that would take Physical movement, such as 
Jumping, Climbing, Swimming, and Evading. 
 When over 200% or more of their Carry Weight  the 
Character is Heavily Encumbered , the Penalty is doubled to a -40 
Penalty and all Movement Speeds are halved.  Every (X) minutes of 
movement while Heavily Encumbered will give +1 level of Fatigue. (X) 
is equal to the User’s Toughness Modifier.  
At 300% or more, the Character is  Immobile, unable to 
move until they reduce their weight below 300%. 
 
FALLING DAMAGE 
Characters will take Falling Damage when they fall for 5 or more 
meters. Falling Damage ignores Armor and Mythic Toughness. When 
Falling, the Character will take 2D10 Damage Dice for every 10 meters 
they fall, with a Base Damage of the total meters fallen. Damage Dice 
max out at 20D10, while Base Damage maxes out at 50. 
 The Falling Character may attempt to make a -10 Athletics 
Test to soften their fall by tumbling. If Successful , the Character will 
halve the amount of Damage Dice taken to a minimum of 1. 
For every 15 meters the Character falls, they will take 
Special Damage to a single Body Location.  Roll a D10 to find what 
section of the Body was Damaged. A 1-4 will damage the left Leg, 5-8 
will damage the right Leg, and 9-10 will be rolled on the To Hit chart. 
 
METERS 10 20 30 40 50 60 70 
DAMAGE 2D10 4D10 6D10 8D10 10D10 12D10 14D10 
FALLING SPEED 
Falling Speed is the length in which it takes for a Character to reach 
the ground before taking Damage. The higher the Character, the 
longer it will take them. For every 50 Meters high the Character is, it 
will take 1 Half Action to reach the ground. 
 
BEING LANDED ON 
When a Character is landed on, they will also take the Falling Damage. 
When being landed on, the Falling Damage will be increased by 1D10 
for every 50kg the object weighs. 
 
GRAVITY 
Gravity can affect how Characters move and interact with their 
surroundings and their environment.  When working with Gravity, 
Earth’s gravitation pull is the base at 1. If the Gravity is half of Earth’s, 
the Gravity would be 0.5 . This number will be used to multiply and 
divide multiple Characteristics and Movement options for Characters. 
 
GRAVITY AND MOVEMENT, CARRY, AND LIFT 
When a Character is in Gravity that is different from Earth’s, the 
Character’s Jump, Leap, Climb Speed, Carry Weight, Lift Weigh t, and 
Push Weight will be modified. Falling Damage is also modified but will 
be modified in a different manner than the other Actions. 
When in different levels of Gravity, Falling Damage will 
instead be multiplied by (X), where (X) is the current Gravity. 
For a High Gravity example, if the Gravity is 1.5  and the 
Character has a Jump of 8, the Character’s Jump in this Gravity will be 
reduced to  5, rounding down to the nearest whole number. 
For a Low Gravity example, if the Gravity is 0. 4 and the 
Character has a Jump of 8, the Character’s Jump in this Gravity will be 
increased to  20, rounding down to the nearest whole number. 
The Character’s Movement Speeds and Swimming Speeds 
will be reduced in Gravity higher than 2 and lower than 0. 5. Gravity 
higher than 2 is known as Ultra-High Gravity, and Gravity lower than 
0.5 is known as Ultra-Low Gravity. 
The following Table will show the reduction of a Character’s 
Agility Characteristic when in both Ultra-High and Ultra-Low Gravity. 
While in Ultra-High Gravity, the Character will take half of the listed 
Penalty against their Strength Characteristic. 
 
GRAVITY CHARACTERISTIC PENALTIES 
0.5 / 2 -10 
0.3 / 2.2 -20 
0.1 / 2.4 -30 
No Gravity See “Zero Gravity Movement” 
Gravity higher than 2.0 For every 0.2 higher than 2 .4, Agility 
Penalties are increased by 10. 
 
ZERO GRAVITY MOVEMENT 
Characters that are in Zero Gravity can only make Movement Actions 
if they are on a surface they can use to propel themselves, by firing 
larger weapons in the opposite direction of where they’d like to 
move, or by using Thrusters, Jetpacks, Vacuum Suits, EVA Suits, etc. 
 Characters floating in Zero Gravity gain a -30 Penalty to 
Evasion if they do not have a Thruster, Jetpack, Vacuum Suit, EVA suit 
or variant, or any other way to propel themselves away from dang

HIDING, SPOTTING AND VISR
 
PASSIVE PERCEPTION 
Passive Perception is used to see if Characters are able to spot or hear 
a Character without an Opposed Test being made, which only works 
within the Character’s Perception Characteristic in Meters. The 
following table shows what the Character’s Passive Per ception is 
based on their Investigation Skill. Anything involving the Character’s 
Perception Modifier is figured by rounding down, and to a minimum 
of 1. 
 
PASSIVE PERCEPTION DEGREES OF SUCCESS 
No Investigation Skill Success with 0 Degrees; loses any ties. 
Investigation Trained 1/4 Perception Modifier 
Investigation +10 1/3 Perception Modifier 
Investigation +20 1/2 Perception Modifier 
 
LISTENING FOR FOOTSTEPS 
Listening for Footsteps can be broken into Passive and Active. Passive 
is when the Character uses their Passive Perception to Oppose any 
Athletics Test for hearing a Character that can’t be seen. This is done 
without making an Opposed Test.  If Successful, the Character knows 
someone is there but won’t know their direction or location. 
 Active is a Full Action where the Character focuses to find 
the Opponent with a +20 Opposed test using the Investigation Skill.  
If Failed, the Character does not think someone is there. For 
every Degree of Failure, the Character will be unable to spot the 
Opponent for one Round , as they are distracted or focused on the 
wrong area. 
If Successful, the Character knows the Opponent is there  
and will gain a +20 Bonus to Active Spotting Characters. 
If Successful with 1  Degree of Success over the Opponent, 
the Character knows the direction of the Opponent and gains an extra 
+10 to Active Spotting Characters. 
If Successful with 3 or more Degrees of Success over the 
Opponent, the Character knows the ir exact location  and does not 
need to attempt to spot them to know where they are.

MASKING FOOTSTEPS 
A character may attempt to hide and mask footsteps by rolling 
successful Athletics Tests. Successfully masked Footsteps reduce the 
Penalty gained by Movement and Ground Type by half.

CARRY WEIGHT, FOOTSTEPS, MOVEMENT SPEED 
Characters carrying over 50% of their Carry Weight will gain a -10

Charge, Run, and Sprint double the Penalty. 
 
LISTENING FOR GUNFIRE 
For each Damage Dice roll that was made in the previous Turn by 
Firearms, the Investigation Test for pinpointing Gunfire gains a +5. If 
Successful, the Character knows the direction and general distance of 
the gunfire. 
 
SUPPRESSED AND SILENCED WEAPONRY 
When a weapon is suppressed or silenced, that weapon is harder to 
detect. These will be reflected on the chosen Suppressor or Silencer. 
 
SPOTTING CHARACTERS 
Spotting Characters can be broken into Passive and Active. Passive is 
when the Character uses their Passive Perception to Oppose any 
Camouflage Test for seeing a Character that is within their line of 
sight. This is done without making an Opposed Test. If the Character’s 
Passive Perception is Successful, they see the Opponent. 
 Active is a Full Action where the Character focuses to find 
the Opponent with a +10 Opposed Test using the Investigation Skill.  
If Failed , the Character does not see the Opponent. For 
every Degree of Failure, the Character will be unable to spot the 
Opponent for one Round, as they are distracted or looking in the 
wrong direction. 
 If Successful, the Character sees the Opponent and the 
Opponent loses their Bonuses to Camouflage against that Character. 
 
LIGHTING CONDITIONS 
See page (p. 26) for the  Penalties and Bonuses for lighting conditions. 
 
HIDING AFTER BEING FOUND 
When a Camouflaged Character attempts to use their Camouflage 
Skill to hide from their enemy after being Spotted, that Character 
must first break line of sight with their Opponent for one Round and 
then make a new Camouflage Test.
